summary: Master the essentials of financial reporting and transparency in central banking. Enroll in our comprehensive training to elevate your professional capabilities
lede: Financial reporting for central banks helps professionals working in or around them interpret statements and explain reported results. Participants examine balance sheets and income statements, connect monetary operations and financial risks to reported positions, and shape clear disclosures for boards, public audiences, and other stakeholders.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals in or around central banks who work with financial reporting, analysis, or oversight.
audience: Central bank auditors and internal control staff
Financial regulators and supervisors using central bank
Risk management professionals in central banks
modules: The Role of Financial Reporting in Central Banking
Accounting Frameworks and Policies for Central Banks
Linking Operations, Risks, and the Numbers
Regulatory, Statistical, and External Reporting Interfaces
Governance, Internal Control, and Audit for Financial Reporting
Data Quality, Systems, and Process Improvement
Stress, Crisis, and Exceptional Situations in Reporting
Explaining and Defending Central Bank Financial Reports
prerequisites: Participants are expected to have a basic understanding of financial statements and reporting concepts. Familiarity with central bank operations is beneficial but not mandatory.
